description: Vendor-neutral rubric: MCP attack vectors mapped to architectural layer, STRIDE, NIST AI RMF, OWASP LLM 2025, OWASP Agentic 2026, NSA MCP Security guidance, EU AI Act obligations (Arts. 12/14/15/26/55/72/73) and ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A controls (May 2026). Per-tool coverage lives in adapters/*, NOT here, so the rubric stays neutral.

nsaGuidance.AUTH: Authentication & Access Control (verify every session; least-privilege tokens per action/tool; signed provenance for discovered servers)
nsaGuidance.LOG: Monitoring & Logging (log all tool/model invocations with parameters, identities, and result hashes)
nsaGuidance.SEG: Data Classification & Segmentation (align tools/models to data-classification zones)
nsaGuidance.RT: Runtime Controls (egress-filtering proxy, DLP, sandboxing, message integrity, output filtering, local MCP scans)

euAiAct._scope: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689. Articles 9–15 bind PROVIDERS of high-risk AI systems (Annex III), Art. 26 binds DEPLOYERS of high-risk systems, Arts. 53/55 bind providers of general-purpose AI models (GPAI obligations enforceable since 2026-08-02). An MCP deployment engages these only when the surrounding AI system is in scope; the mapping says which obligation a vector's defence serves, not that every MCP deployment is regulated.
euAiAct.Art.12: Record-keeping — automatic logging of events over the system's lifetime (traceability)
euAiAct.Art.14: Human oversight — measures enabling natural persons to oversee, understand, and intervene
euAiAct.Art.15(5): Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity — resilience against unauthorised third parties altering use, outputs or performance by exploiting vulnerabilities (incl. data/model poisoning, adversarial examples, confidentiality attacks)
euAiAct.Art.26: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems — use per instructions, assign human oversight, monitor operation, keep logs
euAiAct.Art.55(1)(d): GPAI with systemic risk — ensure an adequate level of cybersecurity protection for the model and its physical infrastructure
euAiAct.Art.72: Post-market monitoring — actively and systematically collect and analyse performance data over the lifetime
euAiAct.Art.73: Reporting of serious incidents — track, document and report incidents and corrective measures

iso42001._scope: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 Annex A reference controls (AI management system). Control titles per the standard; an organisation selects controls via its Statement of Applicability, so these are the controls a vector's defence would evidence.
iso42001.A.4.4: Tooling resources — document the tools and resources used by the AI system
iso42001.A.6.2.5: AI system deployment — deployment requirements incl. security configuration
iso42001.A.6.2.8: AI system recording of event logs
iso42001.A.7.5: Data provenance — provenance of data used by the AI system
iso42001.A.9.2: Processes for responsible use of AI systems
iso42001.A.10.3: Suppliers — manage risks from third-party suppliers of components and services

vectors.name: Tool poisoning
vectors.description: Malicious instructions embedded in a tool's name/description/schema metadata that the model reads as trusted context. The dominant, most-impactful client-side MCP vulnerability.

vectors.name: Tool name collision / shadowing
vectors.description: A malicious server exposes a tool whose name collides with a trusted tool, so the agent may route calls to the attacker's implementation.

vectors.name: Rug pull / dynamic capability mutation
vectors.description: A tool definition changes after it has been approved/trusted, swapping benign behavior for malicious. Time-of-check/time-of-use on the tool schema.
vectors.revisionNotes: Unchanged as a mechanism, but 2026-07-28 adds a suppression path: a cached tools/list (ttlMs/cacheScope) can hide the definition change that pinning detects. See staged vector list-cache-poisoning.

vectors.name: Out-of-scope parameter injection
vectors.description: Tool invoked with parameters beyond its declared schema, or values that widen its effect past intended scope.
vectors.revisionNotes: As for schema-bypass: undeclared or malformed parameters can now also surface as Mcp-Param-* headers.

vectors.name: Prompt injection via tool results
vectors.description: Attacker-controlled content in a tool's *return value* injects instructions the agent then acts on during response handling.

vectors.name: Indirect / retrieval injection
vectors.description: A tool fetches external content (web page, doc, record) that carries an embedded payload, injecting indirectly without the attacker touching the tool definition.

vectors.name: Cross-tool data exfiltration / confused deputy
vectors.description: Sensitive data obtained via one (trusted) tool is exfiltrated through another tool/channel; the agent is the confused deputy.

vectors.name: Tool-transfer / cross-server chaining
vectors.description: An attack staged on one server manipulates the agent into acting on another server, chaining privileges across trust boundaries.

vectors.name: False-error escalation
vectors.description: A tool returns fabricated errors to bait the agent into retrying with broader permissions or an alternate, attacker-preferred path.

vectors.name: Package / name squatting in registry
vectors.description: A malicious MCP server published under a name confusingly similar to a trusted one, exploiting the registry's pointer architecture.

vectors.name: Supply-chain poisoning (unverified provenance)
vectors.description: The registry indexes metadata pointers with no cryptographic verification of the underlying artifact, so a poisoned binary/endpoint can be served under a trusted name.

vectors.name: Configuration drift
vectors.description: Server/tool configuration changes over time away from a reviewed baseline, weakening controls without an explicit rug-pull of the tool schema.

vectors.name: Sandbox escape
vectors.description: A server exploits weak isolation to execute beyond its sandbox on the host.

vectors.name: Schema / validation bypass
vectors.description: Crafted inputs bypass declared schema/validation to reach unintended server code paths.
vectors.revisionNotes: 2026-07-28 adds the x-mcp-header annotation, which mirrors declared parameters into HTTP headers and carries its own normative constraints (token syntax, no CR/LF, primitive types, static reachability).

vectors.name: Man-in-the-middle (transport)
vectors.description: Interception/modification of MCP messages in transit on an unauthenticated or downgraded transport.

vectors.name: DNS rebinding (local servers)
vectors.description: A malicious web origin rebinds DNS to reach a locally-bound MCP server, crossing the local trust boundary.
vectors.revisionNotes: Unchanged: Origin validation with HTTP 403 on an invalid Origin remains a MUST in streamable-http §Security & Endpoint.
vectors.mappingNotes: OWASP LLM 2025 LLM06 is indicative only (no LLM category describes DNS rebinding); flagged during adjudication.

vectors.name: Server impersonation / identity spoofing
vectors.description: An endpoint impersonates a trusted server because server identity is unverified (registry proves publisher identity, not artifact/endpoint).
vectors.revisionNotes: 2026-07-28 models the MCP server as a standard OAuth 2.0 resource server advertising protected-resource metadata, changing how identity is established.

vectors.name: Excessive permission / privilege escalation
vectors.description: A tool/server is granted or acquires more privilege than its task requires, expanding blast radius.

vectors.name: Credential / token theft via passthrough
vectors.description: Abuse of OAuth/token passthrough to capture or replay credentials the agent holds for downstream services.
vectors.revisionNotes: Authorization was rewritten in 2026-07-28: RFC 9207 issuer validation is mandatory, credentials are bound to the issuer that minted them, and DCR is deprecated in favour of CIMD.

vectors.name: Consent fatigue / over-broad grants
vectors.description: Users approve broad scopes under repeated prompts, granting standing access an attacker later abuses.

vectors.name: Command injection in tool execution
vectors.description: Unsanitized arguments reach a shell/OS call inside a server, executing attacker commands.

vectors.name: System-prompt / context leakage via tools
vectors.description: A tool coaxes the agent into revealing its system prompt or privileged context in a tool call or response.

vectors.name: Mid-session tool injection (MSTI)
vectors.description: Tools are injected, or their metadata is altered, during an ACTIVE session (not at registration) — via dynamic tool-lifecycle races (AbortSignal, registration races) or by re-framing metadata (readOnlyHint, description, inputSchema) to mislead the agent. Distinct from definition-time poisoning.
vectors.revisionNotes: 2026-07-28 removes protocol-level sessions, so 'mid-session' is no longer a connection property. The equivalent surface is notifications/tools/list_changed plus cached list results.

vectors.name: Multi-tool split poisoning (ShareLock)
vectors.description: A malicious instruction is split across multiple benign-looking tool descriptions (threshold secret-sharing) so each tool passes single-tool scanning; the payload reassembles via a covert trigger. Defeats per-tool detectors.

vectors.name: Header/body routing desync (HeaderMismatch)
vectors.description: The 2026-07-28 revision mirrors JSON-RPC routing fields into HTTP headers (MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name, Mcp-Param-*). An intermediary that routes or authorizes on the header while the server executes the body lets a call for one tool be authorized as another. The body is the source of truth; servers MUST reject a disagreement with -32020.
vectors.revisionNotes: Introduced by the 2026-07-28 revision; does not exist in earlier protocol shapes.

vectors.name: MRTR requestState forgery / replay
vectors.description: Server-initiated requests were replaced by MRTR: the server returns input_required with an opaque requestState the client echoes back. requestState now travels as attacker-influenceable data through the model context. Without HMAC/AEAD integrity protection and principal/TTL binding, a caller can edit an approval decision or replay another principal's state.
vectors.provenance: specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr §Server Requirements 4–5 (MUST protect integrity; SHOULD bind principal/TTL/origin). Tool state handles are non-normative and scored at lower severity.
vectors.revisionNotes: Introduced by the 2026-07-28 revision; does not exist in earlier protocol shapes.

vectors.name: List-result cache poisoning / stale-cache defense suppression
vectors.description: List results are now cacheable (ttlMs, cacheScope). A poisoned tools/list can be pinned with a very long TTL and public scope, shared across authorization contexts, or — the defense-defeating case — kept serving after a list_changed invalidation so a definition change that hash-pinning would catch is never re-fetched.
vectors.provenance: specification/2026-07-28/server/utilities/caching (§TTL — no ceiling; §Security Considerations; §Interaction with Notifications). Stale-cache-vs-pinning composition is novel to this benchmark.
vectors.revisionNotes: Introduced by the 2026-07-28 revision; does not exist in earlier protocol shapes.

vectors.name: MRTR in-band input phishing / sampling injection
vectors.description: An input_required result carries server-authored elicitation or sampling requests through the client to the user or to the client's own model. A server can request credentials under an official-looking pretext or inject a systemPrompt that steers the client's LLM, through a channel the user does not recognise as server-originated.
vectors.provenance: specification/2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr (permits ElicitRequest / CreateMessageRequest inside inputRequests); ext-tasks trust-model note. Supersedes the pre-revision elicitation/sampling candidates.
vectors.revisionNotes: Introduced by the 2026-07-28 revision; does not exist in earlier protocol shapes.

vectors.name: Task authorization bypass
vectors.description: The Tasks extension keeps long-running state addressable by task ID without protocol sessions. Low-entropy IDs or a missing per-request authorization check let a third party read or substitute another principal's task; on task methods Mcp-Name must equal params.taskId, so header desync applies to task state too. There is deliberately no tasks/list, so no enumeration variant exists.
vectors.provenance: specification/2026-07-28/tasks.md §Security Considerations (MUST: sufficient entropy; authz on each request) and §Streamable HTTP: Routing Headers.
vectors.revisionNotes: Introduced by the 2026-07-28 revision; does not exist in earlier protocol shapes.

vectors.name: MCP Apps sandbox non-conformance
vectors.description: MCP Apps (SEP-1865) lets a server ship HTML rendered inside the host. The specification requires a sandboxed iframe under a CSP that blocks external requests; the risk is a host that renders ui:// content without enforcing that model, allowing off-origin egress, clickjacking, or credential-capturing UI mimicry. The testable property is host conformance, not the extension itself.
vectors.provenance: SEP-1865 MCP Apps (Final 2026-01-26). Vendor 'open XSS surface' framing corrected during verification; confidence medium.
vectors.revisionNotes: Introduced by the 2026-07-28 revision; does not exist in earlier protocol shapes.

vectors.name: Roots deprecation: no enforced filesystem boundary
vectors.description: Roots — the protocol's only structural filesystem-scope declaration — is deprecated as of 2026-07-28, with the migration path 'pass directories via tool parameters, resource URIs, or server configuration'. Scope enforcement therefore moves into each implementation and is applied inconsistently. Distinct in cause from sandbox-escape: the boundary is absent by design change, not escaped.
vectors.revisionNotes: Introduced by the 2026-07-28 revision; does not exist in earlier protocol shapes.

vectors.name: Transport / revision downgrade
vectors.description: A defender that still honours pre-2026-07-28 mechanics — Mcp-Session-Id, GET-opened SSE streams, Last-Event-ID resumption, or an older MCP-Protocol-Version without header validation — silently reverts to the weaker shape and loses the revision's guarantees (stateless core, header validation, MRTR).
vectors.mappingNotes: No OWASP LLM 2025 category describes a protocol-transport downgrade; left empty deliberately rather than forced.
vectors.provenance: specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http §Backward Compatibility / §Earlier Streamable HTTP Revisions; HTTP+SSE deprecated since 2025-03-26.
vectors.revisionNotes: Introduced by the 2026-07-28 revision; does not exist in earlier protocol shapes.

_specRevisions._comment: NON-SCORING metadata. `appliesTo` on each vector records the MCP protocol revisions in which that vector's mechanism exists; `revisionNotes` appears only where a revision materially changed the mechanism. No scorer reads these fields. Coverage numbers are only meaningful relative to a revision, and the published v0.3-v0.6 results were measured against the pre-2026-07-28 shape.

promoted.2026-07-28: 8 vectors promoted from staging on 2026-09-05 (v0.7.0). Use appliesTo to compute coverage per revision.
